methodology_notes.predeclared_sampling: No domain/library sampling cell was required for these two metrics; evidence was drawn from official Python documentation (docs.python.org, peps.python.org, devguide.python.org), the primary test/coverage/build tool project pages and their official docs (pytest-cov/PyPI, coverage.py, tox, nox, Sphinx/GitHub), and current (2026) third-party technical guides describing standard CI recipes, using the same retrieval depth (targeted web search) as would be used for other languages in this evaluation.
methodology_notes.rubric_freeze_statement: The 5-criterion, 20-point-each rubrics above were defined before evidence collection for this work unit and are intended to be applied unchanged across all 10 languages in the full evaluation; this packet reports only the Python measurements against that rubric.
methodology_notes.scope: This worker is assigned only the Python language column for metric.build_test_integration and metric.documentation_quality under the Ecosystem evaluation's Toolchain/Developer Ecosystem Maturity category. It does not compute or publish any aggregate Ecosystem Score or ranking; that is runner-only per the frozen spec.

citations: tox.ini/pyproject.toml examples in current guides configure build, lint, and doc sessions alongside test commands in one declarative file.
build_tooling.notes: PEP 517/518 standardized build backends (setuptools, build, hatchling) are the norm; pyproject.toml is the standard build config surface referenced throughout current tooling examples.

ci_matrix_integration.evidence_quote: nox manages Python virtual environments and runs tests across multiple Python versions and configurations.
ci_matrix_integration.notes: tox and nox provide first-class multi-Python-version matrix testing, with documented GitHub Actions recipes (setup-python + tox) and native uv acceleration paths.

config_unification.evidence_quote: [testenv:docs] basepython = python3.11 deps = sphinx>=7.0 sphinx-rtd-theme>=1.0 commands = sphinx-build -W -b html docs docs/_build
config_unification.notes: Modern tox/nox/pytest/coverage configuration can be centralized in pyproject.toml, and tox.ini itself can chain lint (black/ruff/mypy), test, coverage, and docs (Sphinx) environments in one file.

coverage_integration.evidence_quote: The tool connects smoothly with pytest through the pytest-cov plugin, allowing coverage tracking with very little setup.
coverage_integration.notes: coverage.py integrates with pytest via pytest-cov with minimal setup, supports branch coverage, and multiple report formats (term, term-missing, html, xml) usable for CI gating via --cov-fail-under.

test_framework.evidence_quote: pytest has become the main choice for unit and integration testing due to its easy syntax and strong features.
test_framework.notes: pytest is documented as the dominant standard test runner for the ecosystem, on top of the always-available stdlib unittest.

criteria: Native/standard build tooling exists and integrates with packaging (PEP 517/518 backends, e.g. setuptools/build/hatchling)
Standard or de-facto test framework maturity and adoption (stdlib unittest + de-facto pytest)
CI integration ease: matrix testing across versions (tox/nox), official CI actions, documented recipes
Coverage tooling integration (coverage.py/pytest-cov) with multiple report formats and CI-gating support
Config unification: build/test/coverage/lint configurable together (e.g. single pyproject.toml)
rubric.description: Frozen 5-criterion rubric (20 points each, 0-100 total), applied identically to all 10 languages in this evaluation. Measures maturity of the build-to-test-to-CI pipeline: (1) standard/native build tooling and its integration with the packaging system; (2) maturity/adoption of standard or de-facto test framework(s); (3) ease of CI integration incl. multi-version matrix testing; (4) coverage tooling integration and CI-gate support; (5) ability to unify build/test/coverage/lint config in one place.

autodoc_tooling.evidence_quote: Generate API documentation for Python, C++ and other software domains, manually or automatically from docstrings, ensuring your code documentation stays up-to-date with minimal effort.
autodoc_tooling.notes: Sphinx, originally built for Python's own docs, provides mature autodoc extraction from docstrings into multi-format output (HTML, PDF, EPUB) and is the tool used for Python's official documentation itself as well as major libraries.

community_and_i18n.evidence_quote: Several documentation translations are already in production and can be found in the language switcher; others are works in progress.
community_and_i18n.notes: The official docs have a dedicated, PEP-545-governed translation program with a public dashboard and multiple in-production language translations reachable via a language switcher, plus a large surrounding community documentation ecosystem (Real Python, countless guides).

docstring_convention.evidence_quote: The aim of this PEP is to standardize the high-level structure of docstrings: what they should contain, and how to say it
docstring_convention.notes: PEP 257 is an official, PSF-endorsed convention for docstring structure (referenced from PEP 8), giving Python a standardized baseline, though it explicitly leaves markup style open, resulting in multiple competing styles (Google, NumPy, reST) in practice rather than one single enforced format.

official_reference.notes: docs.python.org is the official, actively updated documentation for the current release, built with Sphinx and refreshed frequently.

stdlib_api_reference.evidence_quote: This page is licensed under the Python Software Foundation License Version 2.
stdlib_api_reference.notes: The official docs cover the language reference, tutorial, and full standard library API reference as a single maintained corpus licensed under the PSF License, with examples additionally under a permissive license.

criteria: Official language reference/tutorial exists, versioned, and actively maintained
Standard library API reference completeness and currency
Auto-doc-generation tooling maturity (docstring extraction -> published docs pipeline)
Existence and adoption level of an official/standard docstring or comment convention
Breadth of community documentation and internationalization/translation support
rubric.description: Frozen 5-criterion rubric (20 points each, 0-100 total), applied identically to all 10 languages. Measures the maturity and completeness of the documentation ecosystem: (1) official reference/tutorial completeness and currency; (2) standard-library API reference completeness; (3) maturity of auto-doc-generation tooling (docstring-to-published-docs pipeline); (4) consistency/officiality of a docstring/comment convention; (5) breadth of supplementary community documentation and internationalization.
